extraction.summary: Zhang et al. fit a kinematic reconstruction of the deviation δq from flat ΛCDM, rather than infer a dark-energy microphysics model. Cubic and quartic Lagrange polynomials are evaluated in z, y=z/(1+z), and ζ=ln(1+z), with equally spaced nodes in the chosen coordinate and δq fixed to zero at zc=2.5; the expansion is assumed to revert to ΛCDM above that cutoff. H(z) follows by integrating q(z). CosmoMC/PolyChord fits use DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 compressed distance priors, and one of Pantheon+, Union3, or DES-Dovekie, with parallel analyses including the SH0ES Gaussian H0 prior. Authors report low-z departures and an oscillatory fitted δq history. The “acceleration slowing” result is specifically a best-fit/reconstruction interpretation: only cubic-y and cubic-ζ with BC+Union3 show a low-z peak followed by decline, and this feature weakens or disappears with SH0ES. It is not a direct measurement of a future acceleration endpoint; q becoming less negative means weaker acceleration, while jerk is not analyzed here. Frequentist Δχ²/Wilks comparisons favor added freedom at >2σ for BC+SNe fits, but Bayes factors favor ΛCDM throughout, more strongly with SH0ES. These are conditional fits to shared observations, not new independent measurements.

ideas.title: Lagrange interpolation of deceleration deviation from flat ΛCDM
ideas.description: The authors parameterize q(z)=qΛCDM(z)+δq(z), then interpolate δq with cubic (n=3) or quartic (n=4) Lagrange polynomials over n+1 nodes. The coordinate u is z, y=z/(1+z), or ζ=ln(1+z); nodes are equally spaced in u between present and cutoff, with the endpoint coefficient δq(zc)=0 at zc=2.5. They assume the ΛCDM history for z>zc and derive E(z), then H(z), by integrating q. This coordinate and cutoff choice is part of the model, not data-driven evidence for high-redshift ΛCDM recovery.

equations.definitions: q=−ä/(aH²); E=H/H0; fiducial is spatially flat ΛCDM with radiation neglected.
equations.domain: The interpolation applies for 0≤z≤zc=2.5; authors set δq=0 above zc.

equations.expression: δq(u)=Σ(i=0…n) xi Π(j=0…n,j≠i) (u−uj)/(ui−uj), xi=δq(ui); n=3 or 4
equations.definitions: u∈{z, z/(1+z), ln(1+z)}; n is polynomial order, giving n+1 nodes; u0 is z=0 and un corresponds to zc, with xn=0.
equations.domain: Interior nodes uniformly spaced in u; endpoint condition at zc=2.5. Alternative cutoffs 3 and 5 reportedly do not materially change conclusions.

ideas.title: Conditional low-redshift slowing feature in selected fitted histories
ideas.description: Among tested dataset-coordinate-order combinations, only cubic-y and cubic-ζ with DESI BAO+CMB+Union3 show the authors' low-z maximum/decline interpretation (Fig. 5). This describes the reconstructed q history and its fitted derivatives/shape, not a raw observable or a measured end of cosmic acceleration. Adding SH0ES moves all cubic best-fit δq curves toward zero and removes the corresponding peak in Fig. 5; quartic cases need not share the feature. The paper does not analyze jerk. The result is therefore conditional on the data compilation, reconstruction coordinate/order, prior, and cutoff.
locators: PDF pp. 7–8, Fig. 5 and accompanying discussion; PDF p. 11, conclusion; HTML #S4 and #S5

equations.locator: PDF pp. 6–8, Fig. 1–5 captions and discussion; HTML #S4
equations.definitions: Difference between reconstructed q and ΛCDM evaluated at its best-fit matter density; plotted bands are reported 68% and 95% confidence levels.
equations.domain: Figures span 0≤z≤2.5; inference conditional on listed data combination and priors.

ideas.title: Model preference depends on Bayesian versus frequentist comparison
ideas.description: The authors compare minimum χ² improvement using Wilks' theorem (Δν=3 for cubic, 4 for quartic) with nested-sampling Bayesian evidence. BC+SNe Ia gives frequentist preference for interpolation fits, often above 2σ, while every tabulated log Bayes factor is negative and therefore favors ΛCDM; the penalty is stronger when SH0ES is included. This discrepancy is model-selection evidence under their likelihood and priors, not an independent detection of dynamical dark energy.
locators: PDF pp. 3–4, Eqs. (5)–(8); PDF p. 10, Table IV and discussion; HTML #S2.SS2 and #S4

equations.expression: ln Bij=ln E(d|Mi)−ln E(d|MΛCDM); Δχ²min=χ²min(Mi)−χ²min(MΛCDM), Δν=3 or 4
equations.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Eqs. (6)–(8); PDF p. 10, Table IV
equations.definitions: Mi is a Lagrange reconstruction; ΛCDM is reference. Negative ln Bij favors ΛCDM; negative Δχ² indicates improved best fit for reconstruction.
equations.domain: Their specified data combinations, uniform parameter priors, likelihoods, and Wilks approximation.

data_dependencies: DESI DR2 BAO distance ratios DM/rd, DH/rd, DV/rd over 0.295≤z≤2.330 with the authors' 13×13 covariance; same BAO observations are reused across all SN combinations.
Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors (R, lA, Ωb h²) and their quoted covariance, rather than the full CMB likelihood.
One SN compilation per fit: Pantheon+ (z>0.01 cut), Union3 (UNITY1.5 binned distances), or recalibrated DES-Dovekie; each has its published covariance/processing lineage.
Optional SH0ES H0=73.04±1.04 km s−1 Mpc−1 Gaussian prior; excludes no other datasets.
Likelihood is summed as χ²SN+χ²BAO+χ²CMB+χ²H0; nuisance SN magnitude is analytically marginalized. Fit parameters include H0, Ωm h², Ωb h² and n+1 node values xi with uniform stated priors.
caveats: Authors assume exact ΛCDM recovery above chosen cutoff; this is a boundary/model assumption. Their alternative zc=3,5 check is reported but not independently reproduced.
Coordinate transforms, node placement, polynomial order, SN compilation, and SH0ES prior affect the fitted history. Redshift-space polynomial shape is not itself a physical dark-energy model.
“Acceleration slowing” refers to the selected reconstructed q(z) best-fit curve and interpretation; it is not an observation that acceleration has ended. q is not jerk, and jerk is not fitted here.
All reconstructed histories derive from shared BAO/CMB and one of three SN datasets; repeated combinations are not independent confirmations. CMB is a compressed distance prior.
Authors quote both a frequentist improvement and Bayesian preference for ΛCDM; neither substitutes for independent reproduction, current-data reanalysis, or physical model qualification.
The printed interpolation equation's summation/product indexing is compact; it was interpreted conventionally as n+1 nodes for an nth-order polynomial, consistent with prose and node definitions.

usefulness.reason: Useful as a source for a clearly specified, prior-sensitive kinematic reconstruction and a conditional claim about late-time q(z) shape. Sol review should verify the interpolation-to-H(z) integration, the plotted peak/decline interpretation, shared data lineage/covariance, and the evidence comparison before any graph acceptance or investigation design. It establishes neither a physical dark-energy mechanism nor a qualified acceleration endpoint.
